name: AME2020 nuclide mass capture: Z per element and mu_min (least nuclear mass per nucleon, 56Fe)

source.located: M. Wang, W.J. Huang, F.G. Kondev, G. Audi, S. Naimi, 'The AME 2020 atomic mass evaluation (II). Tables, graphs and references', Chinese Physics C 45, 030003 (2021), Table I. Not on arXiv.
source.via: The paper itself was NOT opened in this stage: it has no arXiv copy, the alphaXiv tools returned 'assistant quota exceeded' on every call (answer_pdf_queries, get_paper_content, discover_papers), and the AMDC/IAEA/ANL hosts are refused by the egress proxy (CONNECT 403). The TABLE was read in two independent transcriptions: W1 = the tree's own capture extracted/archives/restore-point-2-13/captures/AME2020-TableI.tsv (pdftotext -layout of the published PDF, 3,558 nuclides, 2,550 flagged M), parsed here without gravity.py; W2 = AMDC massround.mas20 (atomic masses in u) as shipped in the pypi package periodictable 2.1.0, periodictable/mass.py, whose docstring cites Wang et al. 2021 and 'https://www-nds.iaea.org/amdc/ame2020/massround.mas20.txt (2023-07-06)'. W1 and W2 agree on every one of 2,486 common measured nuclides to <= 0.61 sigma (the worst, 1H at 6e-6 keV, is keV-vs-micro-u rounding); 56Fe: W1 -60607.16 +/- 0.27 keV, W2 55.934935540(290) u = -60607.161 keV.

published_statement: AME2020 Table I (as transcribed in W1/W2): atomic mass excess of 56Fe = -60607.16 +/- 0.27 keV (atomic mass 55.934935540(290) u), experimental ('M' in the capture's quality column); 60Ni -64473.2(4), 62Ni -66746.4(4), 58Fe -62155.3(3) keV. AME tabulates NEUTRAL-ATOM masses on the 12C = 12 u scale. The tree's quantity mu = (A u + Delta - Z m_e)/A is DERIVED from the table, not printed in it; 'least nuclear mass per nucleon = 930.1746 MeV at 56Fe' is therefore a computation on the published data, not a published sentence.
published_hypotheses: Masses are atomic (neutral, ground-state) masses; conversion to nuclear masses requires subtracting Z m_e and adding the total electron binding energy (AME's own convention; the binding formula it uses is Lunney-Pearson-Thibault 2003, NAMED-NOT-READ here).
Mass unit u = 931494.10242 keV (CODATA 2018), the value W2's u-masses and W1's keV excesses are mutually consistent with (reproduced to 0.001 keV at 56Fe).
Values flagged '#'/E are estimated from systematics, not measured; the tree restricts to M rows.
Published Table I values are rounded to a precision set by the uncertainty (W1 header; mass_1.mas20 differs by up to ~0.1 sigma).
hypothesis_drift: H-AME is two different statements at two sites. massform.py:826-828 DEFINES it as a measurement: 'mu_min is the least mass per nucleon among AME2020's measured nuclides; gravitational binding is negligible at payload scale'. massform.py:493-494 GLOSSES it as universal: 'no bound state carries baryon number more cheaply', and D28's moves (massform.py:2886-2887, promoted into the ledger at ledger.py:744-745) read 'a bound state lighter per baryon than 56Fe (H-AME)'. The floor is called 'rigorous' (massform.py:491) and 'THEOREM' (massform.py:448, :2100); that needs the UNIVERSAL form, which AME2020 does not and cannot supply (it tabulates nuclides, not every bound state of baryon number -- e.g. the Bodmer-Witten strange-matter and up-down-quark-matter hypotheses, NAMED-NOT-READ here). The tree NAMES the universal clause (it is not dropped), but the formal H-list entry at :826-828 states only the measured-set clause. Recorded as a wording drift, not repaired.

ADDED, correctly directed: electron binding dropped (massform.py:2074-2077, 'only lowers the figure'). Re-derived: restoring it (LPT-2003 form) raises mu at 56Fe by +0.622 keV/nucleon to 930.1752042 MeV and leaves the argmin at 56Fe. The floor stays a floor.

ADDED, correctly directed (implicit, massform.py:2083): electrons removed entirely (nuclear, not atomic, mass per nucleon). The atomic figure is 930.4118 MeV (also 56Fe). Using the nuclear figure weakens the floor by 0.237 MeV/nucleon; since B-L-conserving lepton balance can be carried by near-massless antineutrinos and any charge-neutrality or positron requirement would only add, this lowers but does not invalidate the floor. Not a defect.
The tree's restriction to quality 'M' rows (massform.py:2081) is narrower than the table; re-derived: no extrapolated E row lies below 56Fe either, so the restriction does not move the result.
Z per element (massform.py:1753, gravity.symbol_to_Z, first row per symbol): no drift; W1 symbol->Z agrees with W2 on all 118 common symbols.

The pair-floor ratio 1.9975 (massform.py:169, :448, :493, :501) also depends on B = 4.2109e28 from stock.HUMAN / stock.ATOMIC_MASS / gravity.U_KG, which are not AME2020 and are NAMED-NOT-READ by the tree's own account (ledger.py D28 moves). Out of scope for this result; the ratio was re-derived here taking B as given.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested on this result. What the AME2020 authors had: the mass measurements through their 2020 cutoff; 56Fe known to 0.27 keV (4.8e-6 MeV per nucleon). What came later (post-2020 Penning-trap measurements, CODATA 2022) was not read in this stage except CODATA 2022, whose effect is computed: 1.3e-6 MeV on mu_min. Evidence that no plausible datum changes the conclusion, computed here: the argmin 56Fe survives unless 60Ni's mass excess falls ~390 keV (~1000 sigma); the 4-decimal mu_min survives a 56Fe shift of -1.8/+3.8 keV (~7/14 sigma); the ratio 1.9975 survives -1.8/+3.4 MeV. So for the MEASURED clause, M's hypothesis is not supported: missing data cannot plausibly move it. Where data genuinely IS lacking is the UNIVERSAL clause the tree glosses into H-AME (massform.py:493; D28 moves): whether any bound state (strange or up-down quark matter) is lighter per baryon than 56Fe. Nobody has that datum (no such matter observed; stability is model-dependent). Having it would move only the size of the pair floor (e.g. 1.9651 Mc^2 at 900 MeV/baryon), never below Mc^2, and never the B-antibaryon by-product count. The tree already lists this as what would move D28; it is OPEN physics, correctly named as a hypothesis, and this audit presumes neither outcome.
grade_evidence: The result as the tree uses it -- mu_min = 930.1746 MeV at 56Fe as the least nuclear mass per nucleon among AME2020's measured nuclides, Z per element from the same table, and the arithmetic floor ratio 1.9975 -- was re-derived exactly (930.1745822 MeV, 56Fe; ratio 1.9974847) from two independent transcriptions of AME2020 (the tree's PDF capture and the AMDC massround.mas20 copy in periodictable 2.1.0), which agree to <= 0.61 sigma on 2,486 measured nuclides. The approximations the tree adds (electron binding dropped, electrons removed, gravity neglected) are each computed to lower the figure or be negligible, so the floor remains a floor. No moved datum (CODATA 2022, measurement uncertainty) moves any printed figure; the needed shifts are 7-1000 sigma. Caveats carried, not flattened: (i) the paper was not opened at source in this stage (quota/proxy), only its table in two transcriptions -- hence READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT; (ii) the UNIVERSAL clause of H-AME ('no bound state carries baryon number more cheaply', massform.py:493, D28 moves) is not an AME2020 result and is OPEN physics (Bodmer-Witten / udQM, NAMED-NOT-READ); the tree names it as a hypothesis, but its formal H-list definition at massform.py:826-828 states only the measured clause -- a recorded wording drift. The 'rigorous floor'/'THEOREM' of D28 is conditional on that named hypothesis, not on anything AME2020 establishes.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: a ruling that the H-list definition at massform.py:826-828 governs, so that the universal clause the floor needs is not formally a named hypothesis (the gloss at :493 and D28's moves say otherwise). To DATA-DEPENDENT: a later mass evaluation or measurement moving dm(56Fe) by > 1.8 keV or 60Ni by ~390 keV (neither plausible at the stated sigmas). To OPEN-bounded change in the floor figure (not in AME's measurement): observation of absolutely stable strange or up-down quark matter. To a stronger read status: opening Wang et al. 2021 Table I at source (e.g. once alphaXiv quota resets, or via the AMDC file) and confirming W1/W2's 56Fe, 60Ni, 62Ni rows.
